summary:
Growing up in Jakarta, the constant threat of banjir rob (tidal floods) and severe land subsidence has been a daily reality. Living here means watching neighborhoods like Penjaringan sink by up to 11 cm a year while monsoon rains stay trapped in topographic bowls.

To tackle this, we developed Jakarta Earth Pulse: Sinking & Flood Resilience Hub, an interactive web application that transforms complex NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) satellite observations into actionable community intelligence. By leveraging L-band and S-band radar data from NASA Earthdata Search alongside server-side Gemini AI multimodal analysis, the app translates microwave backscatter and InSAR ground deformation fringes into intuitive risk scores, an optical-versus-radar comparison slider, and an RT/RW neighborhood readiness checklist. This project bridges the gap between raw satellite telemetry and grassroots action, empowering local leaders to predict flood risks, visualize hidden water beneath canopies, and protect vulnerable urban infrastructure.
details:
1. What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

Jakarta Earth Pulse is an interactive web application that translates complex NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) satellite observations into actionable, plain-language insights for urban flood and land-subsidence management.

  • How it works: Users select key North/West Jakarta hotspots (such as Penjaringan, Cengkareng, or Muara Angke) or upload radar scan screenshots. The application integrates server-side multimodal AI (Gemini) to analyze microwave properties—such as L-band (24 cm) canopy penetration, S-band (9.4 cm) surface roughness, high water dielectric constants, and InSAR millimeter-to-centimeter vertical ground deformation fringes.
  • It instantly transforms these technical radar signals into an intuitive dashboard featuring an interactive before/after optical vs. SAR image comparison slider, real-time tide/flood advisories, and a bilingual AI advisor.

2. What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Democratizes Earth Observation: Eliminates the barrier of complex GIS software (like QGIS or Python GDAL), allowing everyday residents, local RT/RW community leaders, and municipal decision-makers to understand satellite data instantly.
  • All-Weather & Sub-Canopy Visibility: Unlike traditional optical satellites that get blocked by tropical clouds, smog, or dense tree canopies, NISAR radar penetrates clouds and vegetation to reveal hidden floodwaters and structural ground movement day or night.
  • Bilingual & Localized: Fully supports English and Bahasa Indonesia, tailored specifically to Jakarta's unique tidal flooding (banjir rob) and rapid urban sinking challenges.

3. What Is the Intended Impact?

The primary goal is to shift communities from passive victims of urban flooding to active, prepared neighborhoods. By providing localized risk telemetry and actionable community checklists, the app empowers grassroots leaders to coordinate early mitigation steps (such as clearing micro-drainage before high tides and monitoring coastal wall stress), ultimately saving lives, property, and municipal infrastructure.

4. What Tools, Languages, & Software Were Used?

  • Frontend: React, Tailwind CSS, Vite, and custom Apple-inspired glassmorphic UI components.
  • Backend & AI: Node.js, Express, and Google AI Studio (Build mode powered by Gemini multimodal reasoning models).
  • Data & Satellites: NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) data products sourced via NASA Earthdata Search and the Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) Vertex portal, complemented by Sentinel-2 optical imagery layers.

5. How Is Your Project Creative?

While most satellite dashboard tools look like dry, clinical engineering software, Jakarta Earth Pulse applies consumer-grade Apple Design System aesthetics (clean typography, generous whitespace, frosted glassmorphism) and emotional design integration (inspired by habit-forming apps like Duolingo). It introduces a gamified "Neighborhood Readiness & Adaptation Tracker" where communities level up their resilience badge from At Risk to Resilient Community, making disaster preparedness engaging and sticky.

6. What Factors Did Your Team Consider?

  • Local Context & Authenticity: Focused specifically on Jakarta’s crisis—where rapid groundwater extraction drives 5–11 cm/year of land subsidence, turning neighborhoods into topographic bowls that trap monsoon and tidal floodwaters.
    1. Experience Foundation: Ensuring frictionless core user flows so a user gets their answer in seconds.
    2. Interface Boosting: Passing the 50-millisecond trust test with clean visual hierarchy and high-contrast call-to-actions.
    3. Emotional Design Integration: Building a genuine human connection around home protection and neighborhood safety.
